name: browser-control
label: Local Browser
description: Drive a real, logged-in Chrome/Edge on this machine (Playwright). The agent navigates, reads the page's accessibility tree, clicks, types, and fills forms on sites you're signed into — using a DEDICATED browser profile you log into once, never your everyday one.

config.label: Browser channel
config.help: auto (default) = the wrapper detects an installed browser on EACH machine and uses it — Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge via their system channel, or a Chromium-family browser (Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Chromium) via its executable. Set an explicit value to force one: chrome, msedge, chromium, firefox, or webkit. Note: firefox/webkit use Playwright's OWN downloaded builds (a one-time ~80MB install on that machine), not your system Firefox. The agent always uses a dedicated per-agent profile under ~/.oto-dock/browser-profiles/<agent>/, never your personal one.

system_requirements.notes: Requires Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge installed on the machine (Playwright drives the system browser via its channel — there is NO separate Playwright browser download). Node 18+ is required (the platform ships Node). The MCP launches a HEADED window on the user's display for the one-time sign-in, so the machine needs a reachable graphical session: on Linux an X11 or Wayland session must be present — a headless / linger-only `systemd --user` service has no display and the framework's requires_display gate withholds this MCP there; macOS and Windows per-user services have a display. The dedicated browser profile lives at ~/.oto-dock/browser-profiles/<agent>/ (outside this MCP's directory and outside the synced workspace, so logins survive MCP updates and never leave the machine). The capture-studio tool family (studio_*) is Linux-only and additionally needs Xvfb + xsetroot and ffmpeg/ffprobe (~/tools/bin or $FFMPEG); audio capture needs PulseAudio (pactl/parec/paplay). The studio runs on its OWN virtual display and profile (~/.oto-dock/capture-studio/<agent>/) — it never records or touches the everyday browser.

skills.description: How to drive the logged-in browser: the snapshot-then-act loop, signing in once on the dedicated profile, the origin limits, the headed-on-your-display behavior, and the shared long-lived browser window sessions attach to.

Staged screen recordings with the studio_* tools: the take workflow (start → stage → record → perform → stop → cut with video-tools), pointer styles (real X cursor / DOM arrow / touch fingertip), zoom and coordinate traps handled internally, and audio capture.
